system.description:
Usable by: F (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

A wizard in the service of the Knights of the Shield made this silver ring. By tradition it passes between rangers and paladins of at least 9th level, in return for loyal friendship or an unexpected favor.

The ring lets a fighter attract twice the normal number of men-at-arms as followers, and adds 25% to their loyalty. A fighter who loses the ring keeps the followers but loses the loyalty bonus.

GA p.73. X.P. value 1,500; G.P. value 8,500. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

name: Lucky Ring of the Wild Coast

system.description:
A wizard who loved to gamble made this ring, though his biggest gamble was using it under the suspicious eyes of the Thieves' Guild. It improves a gambler's chances and is prized by the rogues of the Wild Coast.

The wearer may add or subtract one from each die rolled in a game of chance, declaring which before any roll is made. So a 3d6 roll of 2, 4 and 6 can become 1, 3 and 5, or 3, 5 and 6. The ring works only while the wearer is actually gambling and has no effect on hit or damage rolls, saving throws and the like.

GA p.73. X.P. value 500; G.P. value 3,500. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

name: Cursed Ring of the Great Kingdom

system.description:
A wizard loyal to the Great Kingdom made this cursed ring. Its power is limited, but it was well known for plaguing the diplomats of the Iron League.

Once it is on a character's finger, it causes trouble whenever the wearer tries to use his charisma reaction bonus: instead of making a good impression, he commits an embarrassing blunder suited to the occasion. If manners are called for he might belch; at a solemn event, giggle; where silence is needed, sneeze; when full attention is required, yawn; and so on.

A character who makes a saving throw vs. spells is unaffected and gets his normal charisma bonus. On a failure, the reaction check suffers a -50% penalty. The ring can be taken off, but the curse stays until removed by remove curse. The ring can pass through many owners and affects them all equally.

GA p.73. X.P. value -; G.P. value 2,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

A wizard of the Wild Coast made this black ring. He hated everyone in the Pomarj and used it to gather troops of goblins, ogres or orcs, which he then led against the humanoids of the Pomarj. Many other lands consider it a threat as well.

The ring lets an evil character gather a horde of goblins, ogres or orcs, much as a barbarian horde is summoned. The wearer chooses the race, and the size of the horde depends on his experience points:

RaceHorde size
GoblinXP divided by 750
OgreXP divided by 4000
OrcXP divided by 1000

The horde can be raised only on the Wild Coast, and only for a specific, short-term purpose, such as attacking a rival tribe, raiding the County of Ulek or destroying elves in Celene. It takes at least a week to gather, and whatever its purpose it stays together for no more weeks than half the wearer's level. Straying from the stated purpose may make it break up sooner, at the DM's option, and disbanded humanoids go back to the Wild Coast by the fastest, safest route. The ring does not charm, beguile or otherwise force obedience, and a wearer whose horde breaks up will not be warmly welcomed the next time he returns. The ring can be used only three times a year.

GA p.73. X.P. value 4,000; G.P. value 20,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This rod was made for the Prince of Furyondy, but his disappearance left it in the hands of less noble officials. It gives the holder a +15% reaction bonus when negotiating or debating with other intelligent creatures.

Once a day the holder can spend a charge to cast suggestion. The suggestion must concern peace or cooperation, or the subjects get +1 on their saving throws. The rod holds up to 25 charges and can be recharged.

GA p.74. X.P. value 4,000; G.P. value 15,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: M (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

This defensive device was made for merchants sailing the pirate-ridden waters between Hepmonaland and the Great Kingdom. By spending charges, the wielder can produce these effects:

EffectCharges
fog cloud1
spectral forces2
programmed illusion3

The rod takes 5 segments to activate, and the user can move normally (but not fight in melee) while concentrating to keep the effect going. Its range is 240 yards and it affects an area 180' on a side. Illusions not closely tied to the sea or sailing are saved against at +1.

GA p.74. X.P. value 5,000; G.P. value 25,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: M (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

This rod was first made to protect the people of Onnwal from the fierce storms that often lash the Sea of Gearnat. It is also known to have worked well against dust storms in the Bright Desert, blizzards in the northern lands, and winds on the peaks of various mountain ranges.

On command, the rod makes the air within 50' perfectly calm, with no wind at all. It can prevent wind damage to buildings, as long as the side the wind is blowing against is within its radius. It does not affect rain, snow, or solid objects carried on the wind and hurled into its area, and it does not protect missiles fired or thrown out of its area.

It also prevents damage from creatures that use high winds as a special attack: an air elemental could attack normally, but not in whirlwind form.

Each use drains one charge, and each charge lasts one hour. The rod can be recharged.

GA p.74. X.P. value 4,000; G.P. value 15,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: C (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

Druids serving the woodsmen of the Welkwood made this rod from an oak branch, and as they enchanted it they filled it with their awe and respect for the great trees and plants that make that forest special.

The rod can be used as a shillelagh (magic weapon, +1 to hit, damage 2-8 against small and man-sized, 2-5 against large). By spending charges, the wielder can produce these effects as an 8th level druid:

EffectCharges
entangle1
plant growth2
wall of thorns3

The rod holds up to 25 charges and can be recharged.

GA p.74. X.P. value 5,000; G.P. value 25,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: C, M (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

A 7' pole topped with a skull that has a wild mane of white hair and sharp, demonic features. The shaman who carries it claims the skull is an ancient demon's, though many suspect it belonged to an evil wizard who died at the hands of head-hunters in Hepmonaland. When its power is called on, the skull causes fear in any creature looking at it.

Its secondary powers, which use no charges, are a personal protection from evil around the wielder, and displacement as a cloak of displacement (+2 to armor class and saving throws, and the first attack misses) against creatures of the lower planes. It holds up to 25 charges and cannot be recharged. (The book calls it a rod in this sentence.)

GA p.74. X.P. value 5,000; G.P. value 20,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: C, M (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

A shaman of the Gnatmarsh tribesmen enchanted this staff, which has these spell-like powers:

  1. A death ray against one insect or insectlike monster, fatal unless it saves vs. death ray (1 charge).
  2. Animate dead insects or fallen insect life in a 10' area (2 charges).
  3. Summon 1d4+2 friendly thri-kreen (or insects of the DM's choice) to fight for the summoner for 8 hours or until slain, when they vanish (3 charges).

The staff can be recharged.

GA p.74. X.P. value 4,000; G.P. value 20,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: M (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

A wizard who wanted safer travel in the wilderness enchanted this wooden staff. When its command word is spoken, it creates a zone of antipathy 20' in radius that normal animals (giant kinds included) will avoid unless the holder or his party attacks them. Animals of more than animal intelligence can enter the zone with a successful saving throw vs. rod, staff or wand.

Enchanted forest creatures are annoyed by the staff: 75% of the time they leave the area in disgust, and 25% of the time they act to drive the holder away.

The staff can also be used in melee; any animal it strikes flees the encounter, subject to any saving throw that applies, and each such hit drains a charge. With enough time and effort, animals can be trained to resist it. The staff can be recharged.

GA p.74. X.P. value 4,000; G.P. value 15,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: M (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

Soon after Nyrond's troops withdrew of their own accord from the Theocracy of the Pale and the County of Urnst, a Nyrondal wizard made this staff, fearing that other lands might take the withdrawal as weakness and attack. No such attacks came, but certain powerful magic-users guarding Nyrond's borders found the staff useful.

Owning this wooden staff lets a magic-user of at least 11th level attract followers as a fighter of name level does. It can be used only once a year, and the magic-user must keep it for a full month after the followers gather, or they break up and desert. After that month they stay personally loyal to the magic-user for one year, barring unusual circumstances or ill treatment. This has no effect on hiring men-at-arms in the normal way.

GA p.75. X.P. value 5,000; G.P. value 30,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: C (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

This wand has served the clerics and border guards of the March of Bissel. Once a day it can make every mortal being within 50' save vs. wands or become calm and unwilling to fight for 3 turns. Calmed beings defend themselves if attacked but will not attack or take other hostile action. They do not necessarily become friendly.

GA p.75. X.P. value 3,000; G.P. value 15,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: M (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

This wand was made in the capital of Onnwal and has been used against raiding warships from the South Province; its maker was surely inspired by the furious weather of the Sea of Gearnat. It works only outdoors, producing weather effects by spending charges:

EffectCharges
wall of fog1
precipitation1
gust of wind2
cloudburst2
chain lightning3
influence weather3

Chain lightning is like the magic-user spell but with a range of 70 yards. The bolt strikes the first target for 6d6 damage (half on a successful save vs. wands), jumps at random to another object in range for 5d6, then another for 4d6, and so on, ending when a sixth object is struck for 1 die of damage.

Influence weather is like control weather but can only increase clouds, rain or snow, and wind.

Each use may make the weather over a wide area unexpectedly severe. The chance and the kind of weather depend on the effect attempted; if severe weather occurs, the extra charges listed are lost from the wand at once.

Effect attemptedChance of severe weatherKind of weatherCharges drained
wall of fog10%Thick, lasting fog3
precipitation10%Rain or snow squall3
gust of wind20%Gale or tornado4
cloudburst20%Hailstorm or heavy snow4
chain lightning30%Lightning storm5
influence weather30%Heavy rain or blizzard5

The wand can be recharged.

GA p.75. X.P. value 6,000; G.P. value 40,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

name: Dark Wand of the Sulhaut Mountains

system.description:
An elven magic-user who traveled from Loftwick to the Sulhaut Mountains to hunt the ancient enemies of his race enchanted this ebony wand, a specialized kind of wand of enemy detection. It has two uses.

First, it can find the direction of the nearest drow or drider: the user gives the command and turns until the wand responds. Second, it can show a drow or drider: pointed in the right direction and commanded, it creates an illusory image of the nearest drow or drider that way and his or her immediate surroundings, with a vague sense of distance (within a mile, within 5 miles, far away). The image lasts one turn and shows what the subject is doing in some detail, though not enough to, say, read a scroll the subject is reading.

Its range is 10 miles per charge spent.

GA p.75. X.P. value 1,500; G.P. value 8,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: M (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

This wand may have been the very device that destroyed the Suel Empire, or it may have been made to recreate that event. No scholar doubts that its maker was a wizard of great power and violent nature. It is seldom bought or sold, since few magic-users dare use it; often it simply falls into the hands of an unsuspecting spellcaster who does not learn its full power and danger until too late.

The wand calls down a deadly "fire" to rain into a 60' cube up to 80 yards away. The fire does 5 points of damage per round to every creature in it, whatever its protections, resistances or immunities to normal or magical fire, and the damage can be cured only by heal or a more powerful spell. It also destroys buildings not made of stone and boils away standing liquid to a depth of 1 foot per round. Objects in it must save vs. disintegration or be destroyed, burned to dust and ash rather than vaporized. The wand itself is never harmed by the fire, but it has a 5% chance of malfunctioning, in which case the effect is centered on its user.

The fire costs 3 charges and lasts at least 6 rounds. After that, the caster can end it by concentrating for a round and making a saving throw vs. spells. Each extra round it continues drains 1 more charge. If the wand runs out of charges, the fiery rain vanishes and the wand explodes, engulfing the magic-user and everything within 10' in a blast doing 3d10 damage.

The wand can be recharged, but only on the Quasi-elemental Plane of Ash, between the Elemental Plane of Fire and the Negative Material Plane.

GA p.75. X.P. value 4,000; G.P. value 35,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: C, M (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

A favorite weapon of the high elves of the northwest, this wand sows strife among evil humans, demi-humans or humanoids in a 30' × 30' area. Those who fail a saving throw vs. wands become unusually quarrelsome, convinced that their allies are really dangerous enemies. This may lead to open fighting: those affected must save vs. spells at each serious provocation to avoid coming to blows.

If the DM wishes, attacks by a common enemy or strong leadership may improve these saves, while spiteful insults or actual blows may worsen them. The effect lasts at most 1d6 turns, less if one faction has been wiped out.

GA p.76. X.P. value 4,000; G.P. value 18,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Mountaineers of the Yatils made this wand to make travel on the jagged slopes and ledges easier, but it has since become a tool of mischief and the cause of many deaths.

It affects one object or creature at a time, "zooming" up to 2000 gp weight (200 pounds) per charge spent, to a maximum of 600 pounds. The movement is in a straight line, up to 100' (or less, as the user chooses), and a creature moved this way must manage its own landing. An unwilling creature can save vs. wands to avoid it.

By spending twice the normal charges, the user can hurl an object or creature horizontally through the air, speeding it as if it were falling. A creature that hits an obstacle takes 1d6 damage per 10' traveled, and items must save vs. fall; a 30-foot zoom into a solid surface does 3d6 to a character. A creature hurled over a cliff edge takes no damage from the zoom itself but suffers normal falling damage. If too few charges are spent, the results are slight to match.

GA p.76. X.P. value 3,500; G.P. value 17,500. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

First made to protect common folk from the spirits that haunt these hills, this amulet has become a favorite of grave robbers. It gives its wearer a saving throw vs. spells to avoid any special attack of undead (aging, energy drain, fear, disease, strength drain and so on). It does nothing against undead physical attacks or spells cast by undead.

Each successful save against an undead attack uses 1 charge, except that a two-level energy drain uses two charges and aging uses 1 charge per 10 years. The amulet has 2-20 charges and cannot be recharged.

GA p.76. X.P. value 2,000; G.P. value 18,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

The first of these amulets were made to protect the good people of Furyondy, though characters of many lands and alignments have since used them. Hung from a silver chain around the neck, the amulet gives a cursed wearer the benefit of remove curse: it glows, spends a charge, and any curse that the spell can lift is broken. A wearer can at once be rid of a cursed item such as a helm of alignment change, for example, though lycanthropy is not cured. The amulet has 2-7 charges and cannot be recharged.

GA p.76. X.P. value 1,400; G.P. value 7,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Wizards of the Kingdom of Aerdy made this amulet to help in the war against the northern barbarians. It vanished when Spinecastle fell, and scholars assumed it did not survive the barbarians' fury, but tales of its use still turn up in the Bone March.

Once an hour the golden amulet can be commanded to give off a magical aura 30' in radius for one turn. The aura stirs up the superstitious fears of northern barbarians and fills them with hatred of magic. Those of 1st-4th level must save vs. spells or retreat out of the area at once for 1d8 turns; those of 5th-7th level must save vs. spells or be stunned for one round; those of higher level suffer -1 to hit.

GA p.76. X.P. value 900; G.P. value 4,500. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This blacksmith's anvil was enchanted in a shrine of Moradin, king of the dwarven gods. It lets a dwarven weaponsmith make extremely strong, sharp blades. Each weapon takes twice as long to make, and when finished it is either a normal weapon (if the proficiency check fails) or a weapon of fine quality (if it succeeds). Fine weapons made on this anvil are worth 100 times the cost of a normal weapon of the same type. The anvil is rumored to have been used to forge legendary magic weapons for the dwarves.

GA p.76. X.P. value 3,000; G.P. value 30,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

name: Bear Cloak of the Sulhaut Mountains

system.description:
Usable by: C, F (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

Long ago, tribal shamans called on their gods to enchant the hide of a cave bear slain in battle, and the cloak became a powerful aid in their tribes' struggle against hostile creatures and the forces of nature. It was a fur cloak with a bear's-head cap, pelt and claws.

The cloak let its wearer speak with animals twice a day and hold animal once a day, raised the wearer's strength to 18/50, and gave 50% immunity to fear. Once a week the wearer could turn into a cave bear for 1d4+2 hours. Where the cloak is now is unknown.

GA p.77. X.P. value 1,500; G.P. value 17,500. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

One of the first Overkings of the House of Naelex in the ancient Great Kingdom wore this evil crown. Whether an evil wizard enchanted it or it simply soaked up the Overking's cruel spirit is not known. Its powers exist only to restore the greatness and wickedness of the fallen empire.

Once put on, the crown will not be given up willingly. It raises intelligence by 2 and wisdom by 3 (to racial maximums) and grants one level of magic-user or cleric ability; a character who is neither chooses one level of either.

When the crown is first put on, and each month after, the wearer must save vs. spells or become lawful evil, and then save again vs. spells or be gripped by megalomania. Once both have taken hold, the wearer must save vs. spells each month or lose a point of constitution. A character drained completely by the crown becomes a spectre guarding it.

The crown can be removed only with a wish or the equivalent. That ends its benefits, and only then can the change of alignment be reversed with remove curse and atonement; the wearer's personality can be restored only with heal.

GA p.77. X.P. value --; G.P. value 2,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Enchanted in the land of the Snow Barbarians and blessed by the shamans of their gods, these square sails are raised only on the funeral ships of great barbarian heroes and lords. The dead warrior's body is burned with the ship and all but a small piece of the sail. Later, the tribal chiefs can call on the warrior's spirit in time of battle by burning that last piece. The spirit appears as a spectral einheriar (spirit warrior) and fights for the tribe until destroyed.

These einheriar usually have 4-12 hit dice, need +1 weapons to hit, and carry the gear they used in life. They can be turned as special undead. Several villages are said to have up to 10 such spirit warriors to call on.

GA p.77. X.P. value 1,000; G.P. value 5,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Clerics of Furyondy first enchanted this finely engraved wooden coffin to preserve the bodies of the honored dead. Any lawful good cleric can activate it by placing in it the body of a human or demi-human dead no more than nine days and casting bless on the body. The casket then keeps the body from decaying indefinitely, and the dead character can be raised by resurrection after any length of time. For the resurrection survival roll, treat the subject's constitution as 3 points higher than it is (no maximum). Once resurrected, the character also gains the benefits of heal.

GA p.77. X.P. value 2,500; G.P. value 27,500. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This golden chalice was enchanted in answer to the growing threat of the Horned Society. It lets a lawful good fighter become, for a single quest, a paladin of the same level with all of a paladin's powers and abilities.

Only a lawful good cleric can activate it, in a ceremony that includes special vows and the quest spell. The fighter takes vows to the cause of lawful good and then drinks holy water from the chalice, and thereafter acts as a paladin, with alignment changed to lawful good, for the length of the quest. Breaking the vows may cost some or all of the gained powers, at the DM's discretion. If the quest fails, the chalice shatters.

GA p.77. X.P. value 3,000; G.P. value 25,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

The original tribesmen of the Amedio Jungle enchanted this yellow, black-spotted cheetah hide. It gives its wearer +3 dexterity (to racial maximum). Once every 3 turns the wearer can sprint for 3 rounds at a movement rate of 45". At night under a moonless sky, the wearer can become a cheetah for up to 6 hours in any 24 hour period.

GA p.77. X.P. value 1,500; G.P. value 15,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

A wizard who hunted treasure in the volcanic mountains made this red cloak. It protects against many volcanic dangers, and against similar dangers from other sources.

  • The wearer takes only half damage from natural heat.
  • It protects against sparks and hot ash thrown out in an eruption, but not against chunks of rock (called "bombs" or "blocks").
  • A strip of cloth on the hood can be wrapped over the mouth and nose to keep dust and ash out of the lungs, which also gives +3 on saves against inhaled poison.
  • It gives +2 on all saves against magical fire or fiery dragon breath, and reduces such damage by 1 point per die (each die still does at least 1 point).

GA p.78. X.P. value 2,000; G.P. value 8,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This cursed item was made not to harm its owner but to help those in need. It is an ordinary-looking platinum coin that affects any character who means to keep it for himself rather than share it. That character must save vs. spells or be overwhelmed by generosity: whatever his alignment, he wants to give his wealth to the poor and needy. He will never keep more than 50 gp at a time, holding any extra only until a suitable NPC (preferably a beggar, peasant or the like) accepts it as a gift. The generosity does not extend to his magic items, which are mostly useless to laborers and farmers. Only remove curse ends it.

GA p.78. X.P. value --; G.P. value 500. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

A wizard with an unnatural fear of having his head cut off enchanted this adamantite neck guard. He wore it until his death, though it gave no protection against the spells that killed him. The collar gives no armor class bonus but makes the wearer immune to decapitation, especially by vorpal weapons. Full hit point damage is still taken, but the wearer keeps his head.

GA p.78. X.P. value 1,000; G.P. value 5,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

A Nyrondese spellcaster who wanted to control the griffons of the Coruskian Mountains enchanted this green stone, set in a gold necklace. It worked well, but the wizard forgot that he could not ride flying creatures, and he met his end at the bottom of a deep, jagged chasm. Since then nomads and tribesmen who happen to find it have used it.

Once a day the stone lets its owner charm griffons (saving throw allowed). Charmed griffons let the charmer and allies ride them. Flying maneuvers that need no proficiency check can be done with ordinary riding skill, but maneuvers that need a check fail automatically for a rider without airborne riding proficiency. If the wearer rides a griffon into battle, the chance of the charm breaking is doubled (check before the battle).

GA p.78. X.P. value 1,500; G.P. value 8,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This golden holy symbol, hung on a gold chain, was enchanted to stand for the power of its home city. Once a day its wearer can call on the combined effects of bless and protection from evil.

GA p.78. X.P. value 300; G.P. value 3,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This black iron crown bears a large fire opal at the front. A powerful lich made it and used it to spread evil and ruin through the world, and now only the most wicked (or foolish) seek its powers.

Placed on the head of a dead evil character who reached at least 18th level as a magic-user, the crown animates the body as a lich. A system shock survival roll is needed, at -1% per 5 years since the wizard's death; if it fails, the body crumbles to dust and can never be brought back to life. The lich starts with intelligence 0, gaining one point a day until it reaches supra-genius, when it gains the full powers and abilities of its kind.

Whoever places the crown has no control over the lich, so a reaction check is needed, with these modifiers added together:

SummonerModifier
Good-aligned-30%
Evil-aligned+10%
Paladin, fighter or thief-20%
Cleric+10%
Magic-user+20%
0 level character-50%
1st to 5th level-30%
6th to 11th level-20%
12th to 18th level-10%
Over 21st level+10%
Offers treasure (per 500 gp value)+1%

No modifier is printed for 19th-21st level.

A dead player character brought back as a lich becomes an NPC under the DM's control. It may have been the party's friend and companion, but it will tend to leave them to follow its own path.

GA p.78. X.P. value --; G.P. value 80,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Popular with sea traders, this item was first sold to a rich merchant on the coast of Keoland. It is a wooden disk as wide as a man's hand with a small circle of gold in the center. When it is set on a ship's bow and a prayer is said to Fharlanghn (printed "Fharlanghan"), god of travel, the ship is protected for 24 hours: if buccaneers, pirates or raiders from beneath the waves try to attack, there is a 75% chance a misty fog rises and lets the ship escape unharmed. Otherwise the attack happens as normal.

GA p.78. X.P. value 1,000; G.P. value 10,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

A wizard seeking to unlock the mysteries of the inner mind made this small leather cap, which can affect the future of a sleeping wearer.

For each full night of sleep, the wearer has dreams of warning about the next creature or force that will threaten or attack him, whether an NPC, monster, spell or natural hazard. The threat usually appears as a symbol rather than in its real form: a minotaur might appear as a bull or a large, hairy man, and a fireball as a landscape of flame (such as the Elemental Plane of Fire).

The dreamer must save vs. paralyzation to face the danger bravely. On a success, he gets +2 on saving throws, ability checks and hit rolls when the real danger arrives. On a failure, he has not faced his fears and suffers -2 on saving throws, ability checks and hit rolls in that encounter.

The character always remembers a dream caused by the cap, though the DM need not mention it unless the player asks. After the real encounter, the character may make an intelligence check to connect the dream with what happened, so an owner may not grasp the cap's power until after many nights of warnings.

GA p.79. X.P. value 1,500; G.P. value 7,500. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Clerics and judges often own this black eyepatch for its power to reveal the truth. Worn over an undamaged eye, it lets the wearer see all invisible, astral and ethereal creatures within normal sight, and see illusions and polymorphed creatures and objects for what they really are. It gives -5 on rolls to disbelieve a phantasmal killer. Using it for more than 1 turn at a time, or more than three times a day, causes permanent damage to the eye, headaches and other troubles.

GA p.79. X.P. value 2,000; G.P. value 15,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: M (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

This silver oval mirror, 6' tall and 3' wide in an oak stand, was enchanted by a plane-traveling wizard who wanted easy access to her favorite plane, Elemental Fire. Few other magic-users share her love of that dangerous place, though some have found uses for the mirror.

Its command word opens a gate to the Elemental Plane of Fire, through which the plane can be watched, entered or left. Each round the gate is open there is a 10% chance a fire elemental leaps through into the Prime Material Plane, bent on killing and burning everything in sight. Each round open costs one charge. The mirror holds up to 30 charges and can be recharged, but it shatters when its charges run out.

GA p.79. X.P. value 2,000; G.P. value 8,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

The mountain dwarves who work the gem mines of the County of Sunndi enchanted this set of vises, hammers, blades and chisels. It helps any character with gem cutting proficiency raise the value of his work. For a single stone, the cutter may make a proficiency check to gain a modifier on the Gem Base Value Table in the DMG; the DM rolls 1d8 for the modifier:

RollModifier
1-5-1
6-7-2
8-3

The tools also help in finishing stones at a mine: the cutter can add 20-50% to the final average value on Table 34: Gemstone Quality in the Dungeoneer's Survival Guide. A gem cutter with these tools can charge up to four times the normal fee.

GA p.79. X.P. value 3,000; G.P. value 25,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Made for the tyrants of Aerdy, who had good reason to fear assassins, this goblet looks like an ordinary drinking cup of polished oak. It automatically neutralizes all venoms and poisonous liquids kept in it for at least one round.

GA p.79. X.P. value 1,200; G.P. value 8,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Made to protect a powerful magic-user from hostile warriors, this girdle of red silk scattered with golden flakes gives +3 to armor class against swords of any kind. Other weapons are not affected.

GA p.79. X.P. value 500; G.P. value 3,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: M, T (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

This golden circlet was made for the Lord Mayor of Greyhawk and is rumored to be in his treasure vaults. Worn on the head, it lets a character summon a band of thieves, much as a horn of Valhalla summons fighters:

User's levelSummoned

They stay for eight hours or until killed. Thieves of 12th level and lower have average ability scores, wear leather armor, use short swords and carry normal thief equipment. The 18th level thief has armor class 2 (still in leather), uses a short sword +3, and has a 30% chance of stealing the best magic item he can use from any treasure found while he is there; it vanishes when he does.

GA p.79. X.P. value 2,000; G.P. value 30,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

A wizard adopted by the people of the Nyr Dyv made this magic boat and gave it to a Rhennee noble, and the grateful lake folk made the wizard a noble in return.

It looks like an ordinary Rhennee barge, 14' wide and 35' long. On command it moves under its own magic at twice normal speed, 60 miles a day, for as long as desired. Four heavy crossbows are mounted along each side, and more can be added. It has a lugsail that can be raised in windy weather to hide the magical nature of its movement.

The barge magically repels water creatures of less than low intelligence; they will not attack it and get no saving throw against the effect.

GA p.79. X.P. value 2,500; G.P. value 30,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

A powerful wizard who wanted to drive the mountain dwarves from their homes and rich mines carved this headband from the skull of an ancient white dragon and enchanted it. He died in a storm of throwing axes from the dwarven army, but the headband was never recovered, and it is still lost in the Corusk Mountains (or in someone's hands).

It lets the wearer affect white dragons as a potion of white dragon control and gives a -2 modifier to airborne riding proficiency rolls with white dragons. The wearer is wholly resistant to white dragon breath and to all cold attacks, whether spells, weather or any other kind of cold.

GA p.80. X.P. value 1,800; G.P. value 18,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This small cloth cap was enchanted to help the clerics of Veluna heal the dying and wounded. Worn by a cleric, it doubles the hit points restored by any of the cure wounds spells.

GA p.80. X.P. value 4,000; G.P. value 22,500. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: C, M (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

This strip of elk fur was enchanted to keep travelers in the Jotens safe. Worn around the head, it lets the wearer understand how hill giants think. If the wearer can communicate with hill giants, he may choose any reaction modifier he likes, from -60% to +25%. Once a day he can also stir one of these emotions in a group of hill giants:

  • Courage: -20% morale bonus (see DMG).
  • Fear: +20% morale penalty.
  • Anger: -40% reaction modifier, and +2 to hit and +2 damage against the object of their anger.

The emotion can be stirred in any group of 12 or fewer hill giants, friendly ones included, within the wearer's sight, and lasts 2d8 turns.

GA p.80. X.P. value 800; G.P. value 4,500. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

name: Holy Star of the Bright Desert

system.description:
A copper star marked with the silver axe and lightning bolts of Heironeous the Invincible, made by dervishes to aid them in their holy wars against unbelievers. A good wearer gains 30% immunity to fear and +20% on reactions with the dervishes of the Bright Desert. An evil wearer suffers -4 on all saving throws involving fear, magical or not, and a +20% morale penalty.

The star glows brightly within 30 feet of any extremely evil creature (compare detect evil).

GA p.80. X.P. value 1,000; G.P. value 6,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: C (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

This golden medallion was made while Almor was under the rule of the Great Kingdom. The clerics of Almor foresaw great evil coming to the Flanaess and enchanted it to help keep the peace.

Once a day its power can be used on one human, demi-human or humanoid within 30 yards, who must save vs. spells or be sickened by violence for 24 hours. The mere sight of violence makes the creature save vs. poison or be helpless, unable to act, for 2-5 rounds. If it tries to physically harm another living creature, it must save vs. poison at -5 or suffer the same. It also suffers -3 to hit and damage, and an affected character has strength, wisdom and dexterity halved for as long as he or she keeps acting violently. Some spells (such as strength) can help, but only remove curse frees the victim completely.

GA p.80. X.P. value 1,200; G.P. value 9,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

An evil high priest who wanted undead to befriend and control made this horn. Its very name distresses sailors and ocean merchants, who refuse to sail with anyone they suspect of owning it.

Once a week, only at night on the open sea, the horn summons a ghost ship. It appears in 2-5 rounds, coming from the Ethereal Plane into the Border Ethereal, where it can be seen from the Prime Material Plane. It is usually large, with several decks, two or three masts and tattered sails, white, transparent and silent. For ten turns it floats beside the summoner's ship, then fades back into the Deep Ethereal. Anyone who sees it must save vs. spells or be stricken with fear for one turn; the summoner is immune.

The ship seems deserted, but undead haunt it:

1d10Undead
1-21-4 apparitions
3-41 ghost
5-73-12 shadows
8-01-4 spectres

These undead do not usually show themselves, but there is a 75% chance one of them crosses to the summoner's ship. From then on it obeys the summoner's orders, reluctantly, for the rest of the summoner's life or until it is destroyed.

GA p.80. X.P. value 750; G.P. value 5,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

A dwarven smith enchanted this iron horn to seal the friendship between demi-humans and giant eagles. Out of respect for the great birds it is seldom used, but it has served now and then in desperate times.

The horn can be used only once a week. Where giant eagles live, it summons 7-12 of them, arriving in 4-7 rounds. If dwarves, elves or halflings are in danger, the eagles attack whatever threatens them and/or carry the demi-humans (and their companions) to safety. They will not fight to the death or throw their lives away, but they will call more eagles if more humans or demi-humans need rescue.

To keep the eagles answering the horn, those rescued must accept a geas to perform some service for the eagles. If any of those rescued fails to do so, the ancient pact is broken and the horn shatters.

GA p.81. X.P. value 3,000; G.P. value 18,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: C, M (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

A renegade magic-user banished by the Count of Sunndi for his crimes enchanted this conch shell, seeking power over the creatures of his new home, though he paid dearly for it.

The horn summons 7-12 giant toads, which the summoner can command for a number of rounds equal to twice his level. A summoner who is not evil must save vs. spells or lose control of the toads and be attacked by them.

Each use also forces the summoner to save vs. spells or permanently lose 3 points of wisdom. He does not notice the change until his wisdom reaches 0, when he becomes a giant toad. The changes build up as wisdom falls:

Wisdom lostChange
3glassy eyes, warts
6light green hair

15bloated body, hunched back

GA p.81. X.P. value 1000; G.P. value 2,500. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

name: Iron Crown of the Bandit Kingdoms

system.description:
Made in the land of warriors, this metal crown makes its wearer completely immune to these spell-like powers: fear, charm person, magic jar, suggestion and hold person. While wearing it, a fighter gains one level and a cleric or magic-user loses one.

GA p.81. X.P. value 3,000; G.P. value 35,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

name: Iron Pin of the Icy Sea

system.description:
This pin, set in a round case of clear crystal, was first used by the barbarian hunters and raiders who sail the Icy Sea in the foggy summer. One command makes the pin always point east; a second makes it point toward a chosen destination. The crystal glows if outside magical or supernatural forces affecting navigation are at work.

Like a lodestone, though, it is thrown off by strong magnetic forces, and it gives no protection against natural hazards to navigation, such as the gigantic icebergs looming in the northern fog.

GA p.81. X.P. value 500; G.P. value 4,500. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Looters found this hooded lantern in the abandoned castle of Zagig Yragerne, the Mad Archmage. Why he used it remains a mystery, though many suspect it guarded him against the supernatural creatures he dealt with.

Once a day it can shine a magical light for one turn that makes visible all invisible, out-of-phase and ethereal creatures within 50'; ethereal creatures appear as transparent, ghostly figures. The light also automatically turns any undead as a 15th level cleric.

The end of the last sentence ("level cleric") is restored from the book's text layer.

GA p.81. X.P. value 3,000; G.P. value 25,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: M (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

A wizard who greatly feared death made this locket. Two or three other spellcasters have used it since, usually at the cost of some other living creature. Under stress it saves as hard metal.

When its command word is spoken, the locket draws in the magic-user's psyche (soul) and keeps it safe. If the character later dies, his life force goes to the locket (compare magic jar). If the owner is on a different plane from the locket, his life force has 7 days to reach it, or the psyche goes on to the outer plane of the character's alignment. Once in the locket, the life force is aware of what happens within 50', though it cannot communicate with creatures that are not telepathic or lack suitable spell powers.

If the locket is destroyed while holding the psyche but not the life force, the psyche is utterly and forever destroyed. If it is destroyed while holding the life force, the psyche goes to the outer plane of the character's alignment, and resurrection is possible.

The locket gives the life force three spell-like powers, each usable once a day at the user's own level: animate dead (one skeleton or body only), magic jar (as the magic-user spell) and feeblemind. An animated body (zombie) or skeleton has all the traits of that monster but the user's intelligence. A zombie animated for more than 60 days must save vs. death each further day or become a skeleton.

GA p.81. X.P. value 3,500; G.P. value 25,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: M (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

This medallion on a golden necklace was made in the evil temples of the Horned Society's capital. It lets any magic-user with intelligence 12 and wisdom 10 or better cast monster summoning V once a week.

GA p.81. X.P. value 1,500; G.P. value 7,500. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This silver disk holds a zircon enchanted by a greedy wizard, who used it to grow very rich before pirates caught and hanged him.

The stone glows red on the side facing the nearest sunken ship within 1 mile, and blue once it is within 50' horizontally (not vertically) of the wreck. When the command word is spoken, the bracelet raises the sunken ship to the surface for 2 turns.

The bracelet holds up to 25 charges and cannot be recharged. Detection uses no charges, but raising a ship uses charges according to its size:

ShipCharges
Small boat or barge1
Small galley3
Large galley4
Small merchant ship4
Warship5
Large merchant ship6

For each wreck found there is a 25% chance that 1-6 more lie in the same area. Only one ship can be raised at a time, and each has a 75% chance of housing a random monster. Wrecks are mostly rotting wood covered in seaweed: each character aboard a raised ship has a 20% chance per turn of falling through rotten planking for 1-6 damage (optionally, a dexterity check avoids it). A ship broken into several pieces may need a separate raising for each, and a badly shattered one may be beyond recovery this way.

GA p.82. X.P. value 1,500; G.P. value 15,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This item looks like a rusty, worthless piece of jewelry. A spiteful wizard enchanted it and wore it all his life, but, ironically, his peaceful death never triggered its vengeful power. Others have worn it since.

The necklace is cursed and cannot be taken off once put on except with remove curse. Its magic works only if an intelligent creature causes the wearer's violent death. Nine days after death, the wearer rises as a walking corpse whose only goal is to destroy whoever caused its death. It ignores everyone else unless they interfere, and then only until the interference stops.

The necklace's power lets the body regenerate like a troll (3 hp per round), or animate a fresh body nearby if the original was destroyed. The corpse cannot be turned and is unaffected by holy water and other clerical items; the only sure way to destroy it is to burn it to ash. In combat it has 8 hit dice and attacks by strangling for 2d8 damage, continuing each round once the first attack hits. It single-mindedly attacks the one responsible for its death.

Though it regenerates all damage (or takes another body), the corpse shows decay that cannot be reversed. After 15 days, during which it tries to take its revenge, the character's psyche can stay no longer and leaves the Prime Material Plane forever; neither reincarnation nor resurrection is then possible.

There is a 50% chance the wearer extends his vengeance to others besides the killer under these conditions: (1) they were with the killer when the wearer died; (2) they helped the killer and were present when the killer was slain; (3) they killed the killer, cheating the wearer of revenge. Otherwise the wearer departs when his revenge is done or his time runs out.

GA p.82. X.P. value --; G.P. value 2,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: M (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

GA p.82. X.P. value 2,000; G.P. value 12,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This set of many-colored paints was enchanted when the city of Blackmoor was at the height of its power. After the city and castle fell into ruin, the magic-user who made them used them to survive in that hostile land.

Each set holds five applications of each color, each in a tiny jar kept in a box of holding (as the smallest bag of holding). The paint is spread over the user's whole body and lasts 24 hours, during which only remove curse can end it. Each color transforms the user:

While transformed, all ability scores count as at least the minimum needed for the new class. The character keeps all his own memories but has the powers of the new class, and failing to keep strictly to that class's limits breaks the magic and restores the original form. The character is proficient with the new magic weapon (which vanishes when the effect ends) and with any weapons known before. The XP and gp values are per pot of color.

GA p.82. X.P. value 300; G.P. value 2,500. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: M (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

This crystal sorcerer's tool was enchanted to strengthen its power to make dazzling colors. It can cast two spells, each once a day: color spray (as a 6th level caster) and hypnotic pattern. It must be used in direct sunlight; it does not work by moonlight, ordinary torchlight or daylight on an overcast day.

GA p.83. X.P. value 1,000; G.P. value 4,500. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

name: Purple Gem of the Vesve Forest

system.description:
Usable by: F (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

The elven wizards who made this gem, set in a silver bracelet, have used it now and then. The King of Furyondy refuses to admit it exists, since he would rather elven warriors joined his own infantry than formed troops outside his command.

The gem lets a sylvan or high elf summon an elven army for a single declared purpose, raising a number of elves equal to the summoner's age. The army takes a week to gather and stays together only while its stated goal remains. Besides the rank and file, the summoner gains seven aides: two magic-users, two clerics and three rangers, each 1-3 levels below the summoner.

GA p.83. X.P. value 3,000; G.P. value 35,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

A wizard who enjoyed the luxuries of wealth enchanted this purple robe. It gives its wearer the look of nobility: well-groomed hair, clean skin, and rich, colorful clothes of silk and fine wool. Charisma rises by 2 (to racial maximum), and civilized people tend to treat the wearer with respect (+15% reaction from NPCs below upper middle class). Manners and social graces still depend on the character's intelligence, charisma and upbringing. In trading, the robe gives a 20% chance of a better deal.

GA p.83. X.P. value 2,000; G.P. value 10,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: M (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

An evil wizard enchanted this brown scarf to use against the dervishes of the Dry Steppes. The dervishes finally caught and imprisoned him but never found the scarf, and it vanished into the wasteland, perhaps into the hands of the nomads or tribesmen who roam there.

Once a week it lets a magic-user summon 1d4 invisible stalkers. The summoner must save vs. spells to control them, at -5 if good and +2 if evil. On a failure, the stalkers attack a good summoner and simply leave any other. On a success, the magic-user can command a service that can be carried out within 200 miles.

GA p.83. X.P. value 2,000; G.P. value 12,500. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

A relic of a lost civilization, this wandlike sceptre is a 2' shaft of silver tipped with a large red gem. Some of the first lords of the Suel Imperium used it, and it was lost when that empire was burned into the Sea of Dust. A recent expedition from the Yeomanry found it again, and the explorers claimed it came from the Forgotten City itself. Whether or not that is true, it certainly holds some of the greatness that built the lost empire and much of the madness that destroyed it.

When its command word is spoken, the holder gains 2 points of wisdom and 4 of charisma (to racial maximums) for 4+1d6 days. Then he must save vs. spells or be confused until he receives remove curse, which also removes the sceptre's benefits.

The sceptre has 5-11 charges (2d4+3), uses one per use, and cannot be recharged. A character who tries to use it more than once a week must save vs. spells or permanently lose 4 points of intelligence, and must then pass a system shock survival roll or die.

GA p.83. X.P. value 1,000; G.P. value 5,500. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This crown, crusted with small green gems, appeared recently among the ruling clerics of Veluna. The Canon himself often wears it, though he sometimes lends it to trusted agents of Veluna setting out on important holy missions.

Worn by a lawful character, it radiates protection from evil. A lawful good or neutral good wearer gains 4 points of wisdom (to racial maximum). A lawful evil wearer suffers -4 wisdom while wearing it, and a neutral evil one -2. A chaotic evil character cannot use it at all.

GA p.83. X.P. value 2,000; G.P. value 22,500. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This golden medallion on a silver necklace was given to a halfling thief who did great services for the high elves of Celene, meant for him, his family and friends, though no one knows who has it now.

A good wearer gains +20% on reactions from NPC elves; the bonus is halved for elves above 4th level and lost for elves above 8th. An evil wearer takes 1 point of electrical damage each time he touches it, and it does not work for him.

GA p.83. X.P. value 500; G.P. value 2,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

name: Storm Rider of the Gearnat Sea

system.description:
This large merchant ship is enchanted to withstand the violent storms and huge waves of the Sea of Gearnat in spring and autumn. Many merchants pooled their wealth to pay the wizard who enchanted it, and a bloody fight broke out afterward when the deed of ownership mysteriously vanished. Now the Storm Rider belongs to whoever is strong enough to take it and cunning enough to keep it.

The ship ignores storms, always sailing as if in a brisk breeze. Waves flatten when its keel touches them, and rain and snow touch no part of it.

GA p.84. X.P. value 5,000; G.P. value 50,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This woven tapestry, 10' × 15', shows a dark river in a bleak, rocky land. It was meant to be a gate from Ekbir to the lower planes for getting rid of the worst criminals, though rumor says it really opens onto a plane not yet discovered rather than one of the lower planes, bleak as that land is.

Its command word brings a branch of the river into the Prime Material Plane. The water rushes out of the tapestry and forms a river 10' wide and 5' deep that flows for 50' before vanishing back into its own plane. It lasts 3 turns and can be summoned only once a month. The water is brackish and foul-smelling, and the current swift and strong.

A character in the river must make a strength check or be swept along, repeating the check every five rounds or every 10' swum, whichever comes first. A character who fails in the last 10' of the river is carried through the gate into the land beyond and cannot come back through it.

GA p.84. X.P. value 1,250; G.P. value 12,500. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: C, F, T (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

Made from the whole hide of an adult tiger, this cloak has a tiger's-head cap, the skin, and claws dangling at the sides. It was the favorite magic item of the Tiger Lord and the lesser khans until it vanished.

The wearer gains +20% on reactions from the Tiger Nomads but suffers -50% with the Wolf Nomads and the tribes of the Burneal Forest. In melee the wearer goes into a berserk rage, gaining +3 strength (+50% for fighters with 18 strength), to racial maximum, but losing any dexterity bonus to armor class. To stop fighting while living enemies are in sight, the wearer must save vs. spells, or keep attacking.

GA p.84. X.P. value 1,500; G.P. value 12,500. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: M (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

This looks like an hourglass 1' tall. It suddenly turned up in the hands of an adventurer who had forced his way into the Valley of the Mage and came back with nothing but the timeglass and the scars of many dangerous encounters. Many spellcasters have sought it since for its reputed powers, which are rumored to be these:

  1. Vanish time: time passes by a 30' cube for 1 hour per charge spent. No time passes for those inside, who seem simply to vanish and then reappear when the duration ends.
  2. Ageless casting: if the timeglass is held while casting a spell that would normally age the caster (such as gate or wish), the spell instead drains 1 charge per year the caster would have aged.
  3. Restore youth: on command, the timeglass restores 2 years of youth to the wielder or any creature he chooses, draining 1 charge and one level from the wielder. The level cannot be restored by magic (that would undo the reversal of time); it must be earned again.
  4. Secondary power: once every 24 hours, the owner can turn the timeglass over and call up one of these spell effects: time stop, haste, slow or part water. Each use ages the wielder 1 year, or 2 years for time stop.

The timeglass has up to 25 charges and cannot be recharged; when the last is used it shatters into useless fragments. It is rumored to come from another plane and to be impossible to make on the Prime Material Plane.

GA p.84. X.P. value 5,000; G.P. value 50,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Usable by: C, M (C clerics, F fighters, M magic-users, T thieves; sub-classes may use their major class's items).

These colorful turbans have served many purposes in Tusmit. Some have led their owners to great wealth and fame; others have brought them horrible suffering.

Each turban can summon one of geniekind once a week. The genie's reaction and what follows are decided in play. There are five turbans, each a different color:

TurbanXPValue
Brown turban of jann summoning5002,000 gp
Grey turban of djinni summoning1,0003,000 gp
Black turban of dao summoning1,0002,000 gp
Red turban of efreeti summoning1,0002,500 (printed "x.p.")
White turban of marid summoning1,5003,000 gp

The genie must obey the wearer's first order. After that there is a 5% cumulative chance per further order (over the whole life of the turban) that it ignores the order and attacks the summoner instead. There is no way to tell how often a turban has been used. If the genie tied to a turban is killed, the turban is useless.

This medallion, set in a gem-studded gold necklace, is a prized possession of the rulers of the northwest. A warlord will gladly pay full price for it, though a treacherous lord might send thieves and assassins to get his payment back.

Once every 24 hours the wearer may add +2 (or 10%) to any single combat-related die roll, choosing to do so before the die is rolled. The crescent also protects the wearer from all normal missiles, and all weapons striking the wearer are at -1 to hit and damage.

GA p.86. X.P. value 1,000; G.P. value 18,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Elven wizards made this silver whistle for young human and elven maidens. Anyone who uses it well earns the respect of the demi-humans of the Axewood, while any rumor of its misuse brings the anger of many elves, gnomes and halflings.

Once a month it summons 2-5 unicorns, who make a reaction check with these modifiers added together: summoner is good, +10%; summoner is human or elven, +10%; summoner is a sprite, dryad or the like, +30%. If the summoner or companions are evil, or the reaction is poor, the unicorns leave at once.

If they stay, a good human or elven maiden pure of heart may try to tame one as a steed. The base chance is 25%, plus 2% for each point of intelligence, wisdom and charisma above 15, with these further modifiers added together: she is a ranger or cleric, +10%; she is not alone, -5% per companion; she was once evil, -20%. So a maiden ranger with charisma 18 and one companion has a 36% chance (25 + 6 + 10 - 5).

GA p.86. X.P. value 3,500; G.P. value 32,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

A wizard who found a welcoming home in the Griff Mountains and the Rakers enchanted this white cloak. He especially enjoyed his time among the aarakocra, the bird people, and made it to improve his dealings with them. Near his natural death he went home to the Theocracy of the Pale and passed it to a trusted friend, and it has gone from hand to hand since.

The cloak works as wings of flying, except that the wings look like a white seagull's. It also lets the wearer speak and understand the aarakocra language and copy their diving attack. A good wearer gains +20% on reactions from the aarakocra; an evil one suffers -20%.

GA p.86. X.P. value 1,000; G.P. value 9,500. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This cloak is made from the hide of a winter wolf, with a wolf's-head cap, pelt, claws and tail. A cleric of the Wolf Nomads enchanted it, and it has since served those who want the swift, sleek power of wolves.

The wearer gains +20% on reactions from the "Wolves of the Prairies" (as printed) but suffers -50% with the Tiger Nomads. In melee, the wearer gains 3 points of wisdom and 4 of dexterity (to racial maximums). Worn at night in moonlight, it lets the wearer become a winter wolf (with average statistics) for 1d4+3 hours.

GA p.86. X.P. value 2,000; G.P. value 15,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This set of magic hammers, spikes, axes, chisels, files and other tools was made for a carpenter of the City of Dyvers. He paid a great deal of gold for it, but it made him rich in the end. It lets a character with carpentry proficiency build very sturdy wooden structures with 150% of the normal defensive point values. The carpenter can therefore charge double to triple the usual fees, an average of 50 to 75 gp a week. XP value: 2,000.

Besides its armor class bonus, it lets the wearer save against electrical attacks for half damage, or none on a success.

Its maker is unknown, though rumor names a weak, treacherous wizard who looked to his own safety during the humanoid invasion from the Lortmil Mountains. Now it is found only in the hands of a goblin chief. Besides giving +2 to its wielder's armor class, the shield can cast flesh to stone (the reverse of stone to flesh) once a day.

Swimming speed is not affected.

The result is plate mail +4 that lets its wearer save against fire attacks for half damage, or none on a success. Red dragons who see it make unusual efforts to kill its wearer.

Prized by the fighters of the Thillonrian Peninsula (home of the Frost, Ice and Snow Barbarians), this shield gives +2 to its wielder's armor class. Its greatest value shows in mass combat: held by a commander at least half of whose troops are barbarians, its command word casts a spell of berserking on up to 200 of the commander's warriors. They gain +2 to their attack rating and never need to check morale, but have a discipline rating of 0 and will not fight in close formation.

It is made for a human-sized wearer; a dwarf or halfling can wear it at a penalty of 1 to armor class, for a total armor class bonus of 2. Also called the Sword of Neutrality, this silver long sword serves the balancing powers of the universe. Its maker meant it to even out (or, more truly, to end) the extremes of nature, moving the universe closer to true neutral. Only a true neutral character can use its full power. For such a wielder it counts as a +3 weapon for what it can hit, though its bonuses to hit and damage are only +1, and it gains extra bonuses depending on the opponent's alignment:

Opponent's alignmentTo hitDamage
lawful neutral, chaotic neutral+1+2
neutral good, neutral evil+2+4
lawful good, chaotic good, lawful evil, chaotic evil+3+6

Each time it strikes an opponent of an extreme alignment, the creature must save vs. spells or be disintegrated. Against true neutral opponents it acts only as a long sword +1.

Forged in preparation for a possible war with Ekbir, this weapon is carried only by the Pasha's most trusted war ministers. In melee it is +3 to hit and damage. It can also be thrown (10' minimum range, 30' maximum), spinning like a razor-edged propeller and striking as a sword of sharpness, and returns to the thrower's hand the next round. Anyone else who tries to catch it must save vs. death ray or lose the limb; the sword's flight is not affected.

system.description:
This long sword was enchanted for a paladin of the City of Rel Astra. In melee it is normally +1 to hit and damage, but it adds a further +2 to hit and damage against the wielder's racially hated foes: paladins against chaotic evil creatures, rangers against giant-class creatures, barbarians against magic-users, elves against driders and drow, and so on.

GA p.87. X.P. value 750; G.P. value 3,750. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This two-handed sword was enchanted in the reign of Vlek Col Vlekzed. No one is sure whether Vlek himself carried it, though the warriors of the Hold of Stonefist insist, stubbornly and violently, that he did. No one doubts that it holds the strength and ferocity on which Vlek built his realm.

Besides its +2 to hit and damage, the sword lets its wielder choose to enter a mindless rage, gaining a further +1 to hit, +3 damage and +2 hit points per level. These extra hit points are lost first, before the character's own (compare potion of heroism). But the character also loses any dexterity bonus to armor class and cannot control the rage until making a save vs. spells (one try per round).

GA p.87. X.P. value 1,000; G.P. value 5,000. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

A bitter magic-user enchanted this cursed two-handed sword to reveal "the true inner personalities that all warriors possess."

Its owner must save vs. spells or become neutral evil and a lover of battle, with these modifiers by class: paladin +6; ranger +3; fighter or thief -3. On a failure the wielder is always looking for a fight and always fights to the death. At the sight of a fight or a drawn weapon he seldom resists joining in, and even the threat of combat makes him make a wisdom check or attack at once. Only remove curse frees him. A character who dies under this curse goes to the outer plane of Acheron, never to return.

Anyone may wield the sword, but only a neutral evil wielder gets its magical bonuses, and a good character takes 1-4 points of electrical damage each time he uses it.

This broadsword +2 improves its owner's leadership in battle. A commander carrying it counts as having charisma 18, giving +2 to the morale of troops under his command. It also doubles the commander's command radius and gives his or her troops +2 to discipline.

Magically sharpened to help woodsmen cut the rare woods exported from the Lordship of the Isles, this axe also makes a useful weapon. It does damage as a battle axe +1; its +2 bonus applies only against wooden objects and plants. On a hit roll 4 or more above what is needed, it destroys an opponent's wooden shield.

GA p.88. X.P. value 400; G.P. value 2,250. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Carved from the bone of a black dragon, this arrow is +3 to hit and damage. After use it reappears in its owner's quiver each dawn, so it lasts unless lost to a special attack, deliberately destroyed and so on. Once a day the archer can call on its deadly power, so that the target must save vs. death magic or die at once; good characters save at -2. The power must be called up before the arrow is shot, and a miss wastes it for that day.

GA p.88. X.P. value 750; G.P. value 7,500. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

Strangling is the favorite method of the assassins and thieves of the civilized northwest, so a magic garrote was bound to turn up in the hands of Ekbir's murderers. This black cord strikes at +1 to hit, and the victim must save vs. spells or be stunned and unable to resist.

RollResult

Each is +2 to hit and does 1d6+2 damage, and no special proficiency is needed to use them. Using both at once gives the character two attacks per round if his or her class and level do not already allow it.

Rumored to be a sahuagin warrior's weapon, this trident is +2 to hit and damage. Once a turn it can shoot a jet of steam filling an area 60' long, 20' high and 20' wide, doing 6-36 (6d6) damage, half on a save vs. spells. Under water the steam goes only half as far and does half damage (a save reduces it to one-quarter).

It can also be cracked in the air with a deafening noise: all creatures under eight hit dice (except the wielder) within 20' must save vs. spells or be deafened for 2-5 turns. The crack can be heard up to 1000' away.
